data.title: ASN Reputation Clustering — High Abuse-Density Autonomous Systems
data.description: Detects network traffic to or from IP addresses within autonomous systems (ASNs) that exhibit high abuse density — defined as a concentration of abuse reports, malware hosting, and fraud-associated domains relative to total IP allocation. BPH operators concentrate on ASNs with high abuse-to-IP ratios due to their resistance to takedown. ASN-level reputation clustering is more resilient to infrastructure rotation than individual IP blocking, as operators rotate IPs within the same ASN. Sourced from Flare Academy BPH Webinar and Recorded Future TAE provider intelligence.

detection.note: Requires maintained lookup table of IP ranges associated with high-abuse ASNs. Populate from Spamhaus ASN-DROP list, AbuseIPDB high-confidence reports, and Recorded Future TAE provider ASN database. Key indicators: disposable/free email in WHOIS abuse records, low IP density (<200 IPs), few peering partners (1-2 ASNs), high DGA domain density, shell company registration in permissive jurisdictions.

queries.splunk:
index=firewall
| lookup tae_asn_ranges dst_ip OUTPUT asn_name abuse_density_score
| where isnotnull(asn_name) AND abuse_density_score > 0.7
| stats count dc(src_ip) AS internal_hosts values(dst_ip) AS external_ips
  values(asn_name) AS asn_names by src_ip
| sort -count
queries.cql:
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| RemoteAddressIP4=*
| lookup tae_asn_ranges RemoteAddressIP4 OUTPUT asn_name abuse_density_score
| abuse_density_score > 0.7
| groupBy([RemoteAddressIP4, asn_name], function=[count(aid), dc(aid)])
| sort(_count, order=desc)

references: Flare Academy BPH Webinar — TAE provider ASN concentration analysis
Recorded Future TAE Provider Intelligence Report
falsepositives: Legitimate services hosted on shared infrastructure within flagged ASNs
CDN edge nodes co-located with flagged IP ranges
VPN exit nodes within flagged ASN ranges
